instruction.text: Sophie wants to compare the lengths of different pencils. The first pencil she measures is 17 centimetres long. How many hundredths of a metre is this?

atoms.a: She buys another pencil at the shop. The new pencil is 13/100 metres long. How long is her new pencil in metres?
How many centimetres long is her new pencil?
atoms.b: Her new pencil is <mat><gap>13</gap></mat> centimetres long.

atoms.a: Is her new pencil smaller or bigger than her old pencil?
atoms.b: Her new pencil is ((++smaller bigger)) than her old pencil.

instruction.text: Maggie is learning how to save money. Her mum gives her £1 for allowance. She puts <mat>47/100</mat> of her money in her piggy bank. How much money did she put in her piggy bank?

atoms.b: She put £<mat><gap>0.47</gap></mat> in her piggy bank.

atoms.a: With her remaining £0.53 she wants to buy a chocolate bar at the shop. The chocolate bars each cost 49/100 of a pound. Can she afford the chocolate bar?
How much money does she have left after buying the chocolate bar?
atoms.b: She has <mat>£0.53 - £<gap>0.49</gap> = £<gap>0.04</gap></mat> left after buying the chocolate bar.

instruction.text: Phil got 79 out of 100 points on his geography test. What is 79 out of 100 as a fraction?

atoms.a: In his next geography test, Phil scored 82/100 of the total points. Has Phil improved?

instruction.text: Pete wants to ride his motorbike to the shopping centre. He has <mat>1 36/100</mat> gallons in his tank. The trip would use 1.43 gallons. Does Pete reach his destination?

atoms.a: How many hundredths of a gallon would he need to reach the shopping centre?
